faq.q: What is the origin of Alamin?
faq.a: Alamin is associated with Arabic. Alamin is Arabic الْعَالَمِين (al-ʿĀlamīn), meaning 'the worlds'; it occurs in the Quran.
Yes — the underlying form الْعَالَمِين is Arabic.
Alamin can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Alamin should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Al-ʿĀlamīn occurs in the Quran as a term for all the worlds.

faq.q: What does Alamin mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Alamin is rendered عالمین and carries the sense عالمین، جهانیان.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-la-min. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.
